title: The new capacitybuffers CRD will not arrive with a Helm upgrade

detection.reason: this fires on the ABSENCE of a CRD, and every detection kind here settles on presence — an absent row is indistinguishable from a kind that was never collected

quote: This version graduates the Capacity Buffers API to `v1beta1` and ships a new `autoscaling.x-k8s.io_capacitybuffers` CRD. If you use the standalone `karpenter-crd` Helm chart, upgrade it alongside the controller so the new CRD is installed. See CRD Upgrades above.
remediation: Upgrade the standalone `karpenter-crd` chart alongside the controller, or apply the CRDs yourself. Helm installs CRDs only on a chart's first install, so the new `autoscaling.x-k8s.io_capacitybuffers` CRD never appears on an upgrade and the Capacity Buffers API stays unavailable while the controller expects it.
verifyCommand: kubectl get crd -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.metadata.name | test("capacitybuffers|karpenter")) | .metadata.name'  # capacitybuffers.autoscaling.x-k8s.io missing from this list means the CRD chart is behind the controller

title: Consolidation considers nodes in a different order after the upgrade

detection.reason: a change to the controller's own algorithm for every consolidationPolicy: no object setting opts in or out, so no collected field narrows it

quote: This version changes the order in which Karpenter considers nodes for consolidation, for every `consolidationPolicy` (#2962). If you see negative outcomes in Karpenter's bin packing after upgrading, please add your cluster configuration to #9531 so we can better understand how to improve outcomes in future releases.
remediation: Nothing to change before upgrading. Karpenter now picks consolidation candidates in a different order under every consolidation policy, so which nodes it removes or replaces first changes. Watch node count and cost for a few days after the upgrade; if bin packing gets worse, upstream asks for your cluster configuration on #9531.
verifyCommand: kubectl get nodepools -o json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.items[]? | "\(.metadata.name) policy=\(.spec.disruption.consolidationPolicy // "-") after=\(.spec.disruption.consolidateAfter // "-")"'  # each NodePool printed consolidates under the new candidate order, unless consolidateAfter is Never or it is a static pool (spec.replicas)
